card_product.point_value_baseline_basis: IndiGo BluChips have no stated rupee value (re-checked 2026-11-07, W9). Axis T&C (IndiGo BluChip Program Specific Terms 1): "loyalty points and do not hold any monetary value", not legal tender, cannot be exchanged for cash; Axis T&C earn clause: "The bank has no role in determining the validity or the redemption value of the IndiGo BluChips". eligibility_engine.notes: Axis page: primary cardholder 18 to 70, resident of India. open_questions: Earn rule as CSB's documents define it (re-read 2026-11-07): the CSB-hosted T&C, section 3a (PDF created 5 Sep 2026), says the Edge+ RuPay card "offers rewards in the form of Jewels only for transactions on the Jupiter UPI App", i.e. UPI Intent, UPI Scan & Pay and UPI Collect made with the Edge+ RuPay card, and that "transactions made by linking the Edge+ CSB Rupay Card to other UPI Apps will not be eligible for rewards". The T&C names no Jewel earn on swipe, tap, chip or online card-details payments with the RuPay card, so none is drafted (the FAQ on Jupiter's Edge+ page says the RuPay card "is built for UPI" and "The Mastercard add-on is for card transactions (online and in-store) only"). Jewel rates for transactions that qualify: 5% Jewels on all other eligible spend; 50% Jewels on the ten listed shopping brands only if that statement cycle's qualified spend is above ₹15,000, otherwise 5% (5% credited instantly; the other 45% credited at cycle end only if the cycle's qualified spend is above ₹15,000, otherwise cancelled); 25% Jewels on Jupiter Flights. The MITC (25 Aug 2026) gives no rates. The CSB page headline "10% / 5% / 1% cashback ... on all online & offline spends" does not conflict: it matches 50 / 25 / 5 Jewels per ₹100 at ₹0.20 each, and the same page says "Scan with UPI, Pay with Credit Card". Reward unit: no document says in words that "X% Jewels" means X Jewels per ₹100 spent; that reading is the one that reproduces the headline cashback percentages (CSB page) and the Jupiter Edge+ page FAQ ("up to ₹2,000 monthly on shopping (10% rate)", i.e. the 10,000-Jewel category cap at ₹0.20), so it is used but stays flagged.

Jewel value (confirmed 2026-11-07): the CSB-hosted T&C (3A Redemption Slabs, PDF created 5 Sep 2026) and the Jupiter-hosted T&C (page modified 15 Oct 2026) both state 1 Jewel = Re. 0.20 for Jupiter Flights, Jupiter Store, Brand Vouchers and Digital Gold and 1 Jewel = Re. 0.14 for Statement Credit, Bill Payments and Cash/Cash Equivalent withdrawals; Jupiter's rewards page (modified 29 Jun 2026) and Edge+ page (modified 24 Jul 2026) show the same as 100 Jewels = ₹20 and ₹14. One outlier: the FAQ on the Edge+ page says "You can redeem 5 Jewels for ₹1 as cash, Digital Gold, or to pay your bills", which would make cash ₹0.20; it is the oldest text and the T&C prevails. Baseline uses ₹0.14 (0.7% on the 5-Jewel base rate); at ₹0.20 the rates equal the page headline 10% shopping, 5% travel and 1% other. The T&C says the app shows the applicable rate at redemption and the rates can change.

Rates changed in October 2026 and the two T&C texts disagree. CSB-hosted T&C (PDF created 5 Sep 2026, Last-Modified 7 Sep 2026): the old structure applies "till 04th October, 2026" (shopping 50% always, travel capped at 5,000 Jewels per cycle) and the updated one "from 05th October, 2026" (shopping 50% only when cycle spend is above ₹15,000, else 5%; travel 25% with no maximum listed). Jupiter-hosted copy of the T&C (page metadata modified 15 Oct 2026, so newer than CSB's PDF; it also adds the Mastercard add-on): old structure "till 30th Sep, 2026", updated from "10th October, 2026", and travel stays capped at 5,000 Jewels per statement cycle. The shopping and "Others" rules are identical in both. Used: the CSB-hosted PDF (the issuer's own document; effective 5 Oct 2026, travel uncapped), with the newer Jupiter-hosted text flagged. If the Jupiter text is the live one, Jupiter Flights earn would stop at 5,000 Jewels (₹20,000 of flights) per cycle. CSB's PDF shows no change since its HTTP Last-Modified of 7 Sep 2026. Action: confirm in the Jupiter app T&C screen or with CSB which text governs the travel cap.

Shopping merchant cap 3,000 Jewels and transaction-level cap 1,000 Jewels per statement cycle are in the T&C; the schema has no per-transaction period, so the 1,000 sits in the rule conditions and only the 10,000 category cap and 3,000 merchant cap are cap rows. Each Milestone Benefit is then available in the Times Black app for six months from the notification (page FAQ and T&C). Whether a milestone repeats every anniversary year is not stated beyond "until the next periodic cycle" for an Eligible Cardholder who has used a benefit, so is_repeatable stays false.

The Times Black terms are version 3 dated 2 May 2025 (PDF file created 19 Jan 2026); the MITC is dated 6 Nov 2026. Where they differ, the MITC wins. No difference was found on the points read. The statement-credit value wording is garbled in the T&C ("1 Rupee = ₹ 0.4") and clear on the undated page FAQ ("1 Reward Point (RP) = ₹0.40"); the page is used for the reading and the T&C for "up to ₹1".

Network (settled 2026-11-07, W9): Visa. The issuer card page FAQ says the card is "issued by ICICI Bank in association with Times Internet Ltd. and Visa" (the only network named for this card on any ICICI page or document; it is worded as an association rather than "Visa network", and the card art on the page, the Times Black banner image, carries no network mark). notes: Interest 3.25% a month (39% a year) on purchases and cash advances; interest-free period 15 to 45 days on retail purchases when the previous balance is paid in full (MITC). Payment due dates are the 5th, 10th, 15th, 20th or 25th; billing date is 15 days before the due date.

EMI conversion from ₹500 at 15% to 22% depending on vintage and balance transfer from ₹10,000 at 18% (page); EMI or BT processing ₹300 or 1% of the loan, whichever is higher, and 3% foreclosure (MITC).

open_questions: Value of one reward point (checked again 2026-11-07): no RBL document states it for iGlobe. Not on the iGlobe product page (all three tabs), the iGlobe T&C (3.3 and 3.4), the SOC, the MITC, the Cardmember Agreement, the Miles Transfer T&C (only 4 points = 1 mile), the Rewards Programme T&C (RWD 4.1 refers to "the value applicable to the product specific value proposition" without a number, and RWD 3.1 says accrual varies by card) or the public part of rblrewards.rbl.bank.in (FAQs). The redemption screens sit behind the rewards login, which was not opened. point_value_inr_baseline, effective_base_return_percent and the milestone rupee values are therefore null, as the brief requires. A person with an iGlobe login can read the per-point value off the portal.

Network (resolved 2026-11-07): RBL's own network availability guide (issuer page, undated) ticks "iGlobe Credit Card" for MasterCard only, not Visa or RuPay. That agrees with the iGlobe T&C, whose milestone clause names "MasterCard" as the association (T&C 3.3 and 3.4) and whose golf and lounge clauses name Mastercard. The card art shows no network mark and the product page says the lounge programme is "offered by MasterCard/Visa"; the guide is preferred because it is the issuer's card-by-card statement.

Redemption fee: the Rewards Programme T&C (RWD 4.3.1(b)(ii), undated page) lists iGlobe among the cards exempt from the INR 99 + GST redemption fee, but the exempt lists in the SOC (4 Jun 2026) and MITC (29 Oct 2026) name Lumiere, Nova, Insignia, Insignia Prime, World Xclusive, Apex, Aspire, Signature, IRCTC and IOCL and not iGlobe. The RWD exemption is stored (redemption_fee_inr 0) because it is the only document that names the card; RWD cannot be dated, so it cannot be said which is newer.
Reward point expiry: the iGlobe T&C is silent. 24 months is the Rewards Programme T&C rule (RWD 5.1), which exempts only the Insignia Preferred card.
Lounge count: the T&C says Priority Pass access to "1700+" lounges, the product page says "1,400+".
Milestone credit time: the T&C says within 30 days of crossing the threshold in one clause and "within days" in another; the page says 45 days.
The additional 10,000 points at ₹8 lakh reads as in addition to the 10,000 at ₹5 lakh; the T&C wording ("additional") does not say whether the two tiers are cumulative.

Application route: the iGlobe product page says "To apply for RBL Bank iGlobe Credit Card, visit your nearest branch or reach out to your Relationship Manager" and the card list shows only "Know more", not "Apply Now". That is an offline application route for NRIs, so application_mode stays open.
Insignia Preferred Banking customers pay NIL; the draft stores the standard ₹3,000.

Finance charge: MITC says "up to 3.99% per month (47.88% a year)" for these cards and then lists bureau-score bands (above 775: 3.35% a month; 725-775: 3.85%; below 725: 3.99%). The draft stores the 3.99% maximum.
notes: Rewards: 5 points per ₹100 on domestic and 10 per ₹100 on international purchases. Points earned in a month are credited within 45 days of settlement (T&C 3.3).
Forex markup 1.5% (SOC; MITC; T&C 3.2). Fuel surcharge waiver 1% on ₹500-₹4,000 fuel purchases, up to ₹250 a calendar month; the surcharge is 1% of the transaction (T&C 3.5).
Joining fee is NIL (MITC); the first-year fee is stored as the annual fee.
Add-on cards are NIL (MITC "Insignia Credit Card & iGlobe Credit Card: Nil").

open_questions: The INR 1 per point value applies to IRCTC train ticket redemption only (FAQ: "for Train ticket bookings only"). The value on the RBL Rewards portal is not stated, so effective_base_return_percent is null.

The 1,000-point monthly cap is repeated in T&C 3.2 b, c and d, so it is modelled as one cap per accelerated feature; the FAQ speaks of "the monthly cycle capping of 1,000 Reward Points" and could mean a single shared cap. After the cap the FAQ says no points are awarded (zero_accrual).
Which variant a new applicant receives (Mastercard or RuPay) is not stated; network is left null with both variants in verified_network_research.

Redemption fee: the MITC (29 Oct 2026) appears to exempt the IRCTC card from the INR 99 + GST fee, the SOC (4 Jun 2026) does not list it, and the MITC bracket is mis-nested. Stored as 0 with this caveat.

Lounge entitlement: T&C 3.6 says 2 per calendar quarter; the page, FAQ and programme Q&A say 8 a year with at most 2 per quarter. Both are consistent with 2 per quarter, stored as quota 2 per quarter with the annual 8 in the conditions.

Train cancellation protection: T&C 3.4 (May 2026) allows up to 3 claim attempts in 6 months and excludes unreserved and non-AC classes; the June 2026 protection document says AC 1A/2A/3A and chair car only, and does not mention attempts. The newer document is modelled. The cover is described as ex-gratia, not insurance.
Welcome benefit: T&C says "above INR 500", the FAQ and page say "INR 500 and above". Not resolved.
The IRCTC FAQ says the payment due date is 20 days after the statement date; the MITC says the interest-free period is up to 50 days. Both stored as stated (grace period 50 is the MITC maximum).

Railway ticket surcharge: SOC says IRCTC service charges plus payment-gateway charges (up to 1.8% of the ticket) are levied by IRCTC and the merchant bank; the card reverses 1% on bookings up to INR 5,000, capped at INR 200 a month. Fuel surcharge is levied by the merchant bank at actual and the T&C states no waiver.
Points expiry stored as 24 months: FAQ "valid for a period of 2 years from the date of earning unless otherwise communicated" and Cardmember Agreement 12.19.
Interest: the SOC and MITC give "up to 3.99% a month" and score bands (3.35%, 3.85%, 3.99%); no per-card rate is published, so the 3.99% maximum is stored.

The per-card T&C carries no printed revision date. PDF creation dates are quoted in the sources list; the SOC (4 Jun 2026), MITC (29 Oct 2026) and Cardmember Agreement (27 Oct 2026) carry footer reference codes with dates.

Joining fee: the MITC says "Joining Fee NIL" and charges the first-year membership fee after the first debit transaction. joining_fee_inr here repeats the SOC "Annual Fee (1st Year)" so the first-year cost is visible, the same convention as the Shoppers Stop overlay.
notes: Railways (MCC 66, 4011, 4112) is not in the IRCTC card exclusion table, unlike the other RBL cards, because IRCTC train bookings are the accelerated category.

Add-on cards link to the primary cardholder's IRCTC loyalty number and all points accrue to the primary account, redeemable by the primary cardholder only (page note, CMA 12.21). Lounge access is primary only.

open_questions: Base rate (re-checked 2026-11-07, still open): the issuer states earn only for domestic travel (1 point per ₹100, T&C 3.4(a), MCC list) and for flight and hotel bookings on the RBL rewards portal (5 per ₹100, T&C 3.4(b)); the product page ("Reward Points that Power Your Next Adventure"), the application-form KFS, the MITC, the Rewards Programme T&C (3.1 "accrual varies for each Credit Card", 5.4 "as defined in respective product terms") and the card list say nothing about any other eligible spend. T&C 3.4(d) lists categories that are "not eligible to earn", which implies other spend might earn, but no rate is printed. base_points_per_block and the return percent are left null and no non-travel earn rule is drafted. Action: ask RBL in writing (cardservices@rbl.bank.in, toll free 1800 102 6222) whether everyday non-travel spend earns points and at what rate, or have the product owner decide to publish the card as travel-only earn.

Network (resolved 2026-11-07): RBL's own network availability guide (issuer page, undated) ticks World Safari Lite for MasterCard, RuPay and Visa, so it is recorded as a multi-network card with card_product.network left null. Which network a new customer is issued is not stated; the T&C only says "MasterCard/RuPay/VISA" generically. On the RuPay variant, the Rewards Programme T&C (5.4) says offline UPI transactions under ₹2,000 at small merchants earn no base points, voucher or milestone benefits.
International travel: only "domestic travel" earns 1 point per ₹100; whether international airline, hotel or transport spend earns anything is not stated.

Welcome benefit: T&C 3.2(c) conditions the voucher on paying the "first month membership fees", while the page says the annual fee; the card carries an annual fee. Ixigo offer valid to 31 Dec 2026 per the welcome T&C.
Milestone tiers: T&C 3.5(b) says "additional 10,000" points at ₹5 lakh; it is not stated whether this adds to the 5,000 at ₹2.5 lakh. Rupee values use the ₹0.05 baseline (₹0.25 would be 5x).

Lounge: T&C 3.3.1 requires ₹50,000 spend in the same calendar quarter for the international voucher; 3.3.2 and the page tie the domestic visit to the previous quarter. The page says one visit per quarter "within and outside India".
Points value for flights and hotels is ₹0.25, so the 5X earn is a 1.25% return only if redeemed on flights or hotels; at ₹0.05 it is 0.25%.
Reward point expiry is the Rewards Programme T&C rule (24 months, RWD 5.1); the product T&C is silent.

Finance charge: MITC says "up to 3.99% per month (47.88% a year)" for these cards and then lists bureau-score bands (above 775: 3.35% a month; 725-775: 3.85%; below 725: 3.99%). The draft stores the 3.99% maximum.

open_questions: HELD: no reward rate for the current card is published. Re-read in wave 3 (W11, 2026-11-07): the product page, its Top Benefits slider (earn cashbacks, works everywhere, 1-click controls on the app, scan and pay for UPI: all images with headline text only), the What-comes-with-the-card items (lifetime free, works everywhere, 1% fuel surcharge waiver, lounge), the 7 FAQs, the usage guide, MITC V18 (the "English" MITC link on the page resolves to it; no Zagg or Rio coin terms in it) and the Cardmember Agreement state no cashback or coin rate. The only rate is the footnote for cards issued before 10 Jan 2025 (0.5 Rio coins per ₹50 on non-UPI and 1.5 Rio coins per ₹50 on UPI, outside exclusion categories). The page says any programme run by the Zagg app is the app provider's sole responsibility, so the current cashback programme sits outside YES documents. The value of a Rio coin is not stated. No reward rules are written. To unblock: ask YES BANK or Zagg for the Zagg card rewards terms.

Network (settled 2026-11-07, W11): RuPay, from card art on YES BANK's own Zagg pages (the usage guide PDF, the hero banner and the Top Benefits slide all show "YES BANK" and the RuPay logo). The product FAQ also says the card links to UPI apps ("NPCI recognised TPAPs"). The MITC and KFS do not name the network.

RIO and Zagg: the issuer lists one product. The page assets are named "rio_*" and the pre-10-Jan-2025 footnote speaks of Rio coins, so Rio is the earlier name of the same card; the old co-brand MITC (undated Mizo translation) lists "Rio" and the current MITC lists "Zagg". Treated as one card.
Lounge: two domestic visits a calendar quarter (page, listing) with a ₹50,000 prior-quarter spend condition (MITC 3(r), Lounge Program). Whether any international lounge access exists is not stated.
Fuel surcharge waiver: from 15 Jun 2026 ₹400 to ₹5,000 and ₹250 per statement cycle (MITC 4, KFS); the page glossary says the cap is ₹250 and states no range. No waiver on UPI fuel transactions.
notes: Forex mark-up is 3.50% (MITC and KFS list Zagg with BYOC / EMI / Wellness / Novio / Max).

rules: Late payment charge: no charge if the current outstanding (statement balance + unbilled) is up to ₹500; above ₹500, 10% of the statement balance or ₹1,350, whichever is lower, per statement (MITC 3(b), KFS).

Auto-debit / payment return failure: from 15 Jun 2026, 2.5% or ₹500 whichever is higher on the net payable amount, capped at ₹5,000 per customer per statement (before that 2% or ₹450, cap ₹1,500); cheque return ₹450 (MITC 3(d)).
Overlimit: ₹550 + GST per transaction that exceeds the limit (facility reintroduced 1 Jun 2026) (MITC 3(c)).

Cash advance: from 15 Jun 2026, 2.5% or ₹650 whichever is higher; before that 2.5% or ₹500; not applicable to virtual cards; cash withdrawal suspended for the first 6 months after onboarding; limit up to 30% of the credit limit (MITC 3(a), 5).
